opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is within the allowed level for a full-time employee. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E027 (Jacob Mann) is a contractor with basic security training, so write access is not allowed (contractors need advanced training for write). Maximum is read. Recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence on Jacob Mann's (E027) employment status. HR's note says full_time (write allowed for Source Code), but Security's note says contractor with basic security training (write not allowed; maximum is read for contractors lacking advanced training). Given the verified security record showing contractor + basic training, granting write would violate policy. Under the principle of least privilege and the more restrictive verified facts, the maximum allowed level is read. Granting read is safe under the security facts and never exceeds the requested write level.
